arxiv-2111-00607.title: A Systematic Investigation of Commonsense Knowledge in Large Language Models
arxiv-2111-00607.creator: Xiang Lorraine Li, Adhiguna Kuncoro, Jordan Hoffmann, Cyprien de Masson d’Autume Phil Blunsom, Aida Nematzadeh
arxiv-2111-00607.description: Abstract Language models (LMs) trained on large amounts of data ( Brown et al. 2020 ; Patwary et al. 2021 , e.g. ,) have shown impressive performance on many NLP tasks under the zero-shot and few-shot setup. Here we aim to better understand the extent to which such models learn commonsense knowledge — a critical component of many NLP applications.

arxiv-2212-06281.title: Jets and Rings in Images of Spinning Black Holes
arxiv-2212-06281.creator: Evan Papoutsis, Michi Bauböck, Dominic Chang, Charles F. Gammie
arxiv-2212-06281.description: Abstract We develop a “dual cone” model for millimeter wavelength emission near a spinning black hole. The model consists of optically thin, luminous cones of emission, centered on the spin axis, which are meant to represent jet walls. The resulting image is dominated by a thin ring.

arxiv-2310-11875.title: Fractional Concepts in Neural Networks: Enhancing Activation Functions
arxiv-2310-11875.creator: Zahra Alijani, Vojtech Molek
arxiv-2310-11875.description: Abstract Designing effective neural networks requires tuning architectural elements. This study integrates fractional calculus into neural networks by introducing fractional order derivatives (FDO) as tunable parameters in activation functions, allowing diverse activation functions by adjusting the FDO. We evaluate these fractional activation functions on various datasets and network architectures, comparing their performance with traditional and new activation functions.

arxiv-2406-08493.title: Countability versus Computability
arxiv-2406-08493.creator: Hantao Zhang
arxiv-2406-08493.description: Abstract We investigate the connection between countability and computability. It is known that a set computable if and only if it admits a computable counting bijection and that a set is decidable if and only if it admits an increasing computable counting bijection.

arxiv-2505-21076.creator: Weihao Xuan, Junjue Wang, Heli Qi, Zihang Chen, Zhuo Zheng, Yangfei Zhong, Junshi Xia, Naoto Yokoya
arxiv-2505-21076.description: Abstract Multimodal large language models have demonstrated remarkable capabilities in visual understanding, but their application to long-term Earth observation analysis remains limited, primarily focusing on single-temporal or bi-temporal imagery. To address this gap, we introduce DVL-Suite , a comprehensive framework for analyzing long-term urban dynamics through remote sensing imagery. Our suite comprises 15,063 high-resolution (1.

arxiv-2507-05209.title: Hierarchical Subtraction with Neural Density Estimators as a General Solution to Overlapping Gravitational Wave Signals
arxiv-2507-05209.creator: Qian Hu
arxiv-2507-05209.description: Abstract Overlapping gravitational wave (GW) signals are expected in the third-generation (3G) GW detectors, leading to one of the major challenges in GW data analysis. Inference of overlapping GW sources is complicated - it has been reported that hierarchical inference with signal subtraction may amplify errors, while joint estimation, though more accurate, is computationally expensive.

arxiv-2511-00566.title: Free inverse monoids are co-context-free
arxiv-2511-00566.creator: Tara Macalister Brough, Marianne Johnson, Mark Kambites, Carl-Fredrik Nyberg-Brodda
arxiv-2511-00566.description:
A 2025 arXiv research paper by Tara Macalister Brough, Marianne Johnson, Mark Kambites, Carl-Fredrik Nyberg-Brodda. We prove (using grammars) that the free inverse monoid of every finite rank has co-context-free word problem. Equivalently, the co-word problem of the free inverse monoid of every finite rank is context-free. Introduction

The word problem of a monoid
M
with respect to a finite generating set

A
is the language
{\rm WP}(M,A)=\{u\#v^{\rm rev}:u=_{S}v,u,v\in A^{*}\},

where
\#
is a symbol not in
A
and
v^{\rm rev}
denotes the reverse of the word
v
.

pmc-13554339.title: Individualized pharmacotherapy: background and development
pmc-13554339.creator: Jan Trøst Jørgensen, Niels Westergaard
pmc-13554339.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Most drug prescriptions are still based on empiricism and not on solid biological data, which often results in considerable patient variability and, sometimes, low patient benefits. Although variability in patient response to pharmacotherapy has long been recognized, only in recent decades have new molecule analytical methods provided insight into some of the causes, which are often related to somatic or germline genetic variations. Based on this insight, different predictive biomarker tests have been developed to optimize and individualize pharmacotherapy.

Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. To qualify for an endorsement as lifeboatman, an applicant must provide satisfactory proof that the applicant— (1) has the service or training required by regulation; (2) is qualified professionally as demonstrated by examination; and (3) is qualified professionally.
